_readme: PROVISIONING MANIFEST — the single source of truth for every third-party tool
Claude Station installs on a user's behalf. Nothing here is fetched at session
start: a tool is installed ONCE, at provision time, into a durable location
(a baked image layer for isolation:container, a station-owned directory for
isolation:direct), and every session afterwards just executes it.
CHANGING THIS FILE CHANGES THE IMAGE IDENTITY. src/server/provisioning.ts
hashes this file together with the Dockerfile, and container-manager.ts puts
that hash in the image tag — so a version bump here yields a different
artifact, the drift check sees it, and the container is recreated. That is
deliberate: a pin nobody rebuilds on is not a pin, it is a comment.
A version bump NEVER installs itself. It marks the existing install stale and
waits for an explicit, user-initiated provision/update.
FEAT-151 — the Claude CLI baked into every per-project CONTAINER image.
Container sessions run THIS CLI (docker exec claude), not the host's and
not the SDK-bundled one — see src/server/container/Dockerfile and
CONTAINER_CLAUDE_BIN in container-manager.ts.
appliesTo:['container'] keeps it OUT of host provisioning: host (direct)
sessions run the CLI bundled inside @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk, updated
via the Runtime settings pane (runtime-update.ts), never this pin.
THE TARGET: this version must track the CLI the host SDK bundles, because a
container session still runs the host SDK JS across the docker boundary and
the two ship version-locked (finding #7). The Runtime pane's 'update
container CLI' writes the host SDK's bundled --version here, which changes
provisionHash() → a new image tag → the drift check rebuilds. A bump never
force-restarts a running container: new containers pick up the new image.

browserNote: @playwright/mcp launches a browser LAZILY (first browser_navigate), not at
server start — the MCP server lists its ~24 tools with no browser and no
network. Its DEFAULT is the 'chrome' channel (a SYSTEM Google Chrome at
/opt/google/chrome/chrome); with no browser present it returns an actionable
error telling you to install one — it does NOT auto-fetch at session start.
src/server/tools.ts points direct-isolation sessions at an existing browser
so a real navigate works fully offline. CONTAINER isolation gets the browser
baked below — see `.browser` — because 'no browser in the container' was not a
neutral gap: BUG-151 showed a session reach for Playwright first (correctly),
get this exact error, and fall back to the HEADFUL stealth browser, putting a
window in the user's workspace for a job that should have been invisible.

_readme: BUG-151 — the browser Playwright drives inside the container image.
Installed at BUILD time by playwright-core's own installer (the same
playwright-core the pinned @playwright/mcp depends on, so the build is
resolved by the MCP pin above, not by a floating tag). Nothing is fetched
at session start: src/server/tools.ts passes `--browser chromium` and the
image exports PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH, so the MCP server finds a browser
that is already on disk. If it is missing, the error is honest and the
answer is to rebuild the image — never `playwright install` from a session.
browser.name: chromium
browser.resolvedBy: the playwright-core version depended on by @playwright/mcp above
